title: SIRIUS – A study of a new combination therapy in patients recently diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension
official: SIRIUS - A prospective, non-randomized, open-label, proof-of-concept study of initial combination therapy with an endothelin receptor antagonist, a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor and sotatercept in patients with newly diagnosed pulmonary arterial hypertension
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the feasibility of recruitment, safety and treatment compliance of 24 weeks of triple combination therapy with an ERA, a PDE5i, and Sotatercept on pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) in patients with newly diagnosed PAH.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age 18-70 years
2. Treatment-naïve patients diagnosed within 12 weeks prior to screening with I/H/D-PAH or PAH associated with corrected congenital heart disease (≥12 months after correction), irrespective of their WHO functional class at baseline.
3. Patients who have been treated with ERA/PDE5i are eligible if treatment started after RHC which is not older than six weeks.
4. PVR >5 WU, mPAP ≥35 mmHg and PAWP or LVEDP ≤15 mmHg at PAH diagnosis
5. Signed written informed consent
6. For women of childbearing potential: A negative result in highly sensitive pregnancy test and willingness of additional monthly pregnancy testing during the duration of the trial and until the end of relevant systemic exposure. End of relevant systemic exposure for the IMP Sotatercept is achieved after 112 days after the last administration of Sotatercept.
7. For women of childbearing potential (WOCBP): a highly effective method of contraception* preferably with low user dependency, that has been in use for at least eight weeks prior inclusion in the study and continued during treatment and until the end of relevant systemic exposure. End of relevant systemic exposure for the IMP Sotatercept is achieved 112 days after the last administration of Sotatercept. *According to the „Recommendations related to contraception and pregnancy testing in clinical trials Version 1.2“ of the CTCG Clinical Trials Coordination Group - methods that can achieve a failure rate of less than 1% per year when used consistently and correctly are considered as highly effective birth control methods. Such methods include: - combined (estrogen and progestogen containing) hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation 1 : o oral o intravaginal o transdermal - progestogen-only hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation  : o oral o injectable o implantable  - intrauterine device (IUD)  - intrauterine hormone-releasing system (IUS)  - bilateral tubal occlusion  - vasectomised partner  - sexual abstinence
8. Willingness of males who are sexually active with a female partner of childbearing potential to use a condom. In addition, contraception of the female partner during treatment and until the end of relevant systemic exposure in WOCBP. End of relevant systemic exposure for the IMP Sotatercept is achieved after 112 days after the last administration of Sotatercept.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Other forms of PH or PAH.
2. eGFR <30 ml/min/m2 at screening
3. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
4. Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the other excipients
5. Use of PAH medications for more than 6 weeks prior to screening.
6. PAH diagnosis more than 3 months prior to screening
7. Symptoms or signs of clinically relevant lung disease, including TLC <70%, FEV1/FVC <60%, and DLCO (Diffusing Capacity of the Lungs for Carbon Monoxide) <45%, respectively
8. Signs of left heart failure with reduced or preserved ejection fraction, including LVEF <50%, LAVI >34 ml/m2, E/é ≥15, or permanent atrial fibrillation, respectively
9. Hemoglobin <8 g/dL or >17 g/dL for women and >19g/dL for men at screening
10. Thrombocyte count <80.000/µl at screening
11. High bleeding risk by the discretion of the investigator
12. Ongoing therapy with prostacyclin analogues or prostacyclin receptor agonists
